prs.body: ## Purpose Fixes #57017 DeepSeek-V2-Lite with `--quantization fp8` on sm89 (`TRITON_MLA`) returns NaN logits for every request once three or more sequences share one CUDA-graph decode batch. Eager / `cudagraph_mode: NONE` are fine; `--max-num-seqs 2` sidesteps it. ### Root cause 1. Default CUDA-graph capture sizes are `[1, 2, 4, 8, ...]`, so a 3-sequence decode batch is padded to 4. items.title: [Bug]: Mixed prompt embedding masks are omitted from prefix cache keys, causing incorrect outputs
items.body: With `enable_prompt_embeds=True` and `enable_prefix_caching=True`, valid inputs with the same token IDs and supplied embedding tensor but different `prompt_is_token_ids` masks can reuse KV computed for a different effective input. The request succeeds, but its deterministic output depends on an earlier request's cache contents. `prompt_is_token_ids[i]` selects either the model's learned embedding for the token ID (`True`) or the supplied embedding row (`False`). The prefix-cache key hashes the normalized token IDs and supplied tensor, but omits that selection mask. Embedding-backed positions are normalized to token ID 0, which is also a valid vocabulary ID. In the reproducer, B alone generates `[9, 0] * 8`. After caching A, the **identical B** incorrectly hits 32 cached tokens and generates `[753] * 16`. Repeating A itself correctly hits 32 tokens. ### Scope This is a functional correctness issue in the combination of mixed prompt embeddings and local prefix caching. The reproducer uses the public offline input interface, without external KV connectors, LoRA, concurrency, or stochastic sampling. It does not establish a failure in ordinary text-only requests or a production occurrence rate. The standard chat renderer zero-fills supplied-tensor rows at text positions, which narrows the conditions for two rendered requests to have identical tensor bytes and different masks. A complete HTTP Chat Completions reproduction is not claimed here. items.body: ### my environment - GPU: NVIDIA H20 (Hopper, SM90) - Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (hybrid-GDN: 24 linear_attn layers + 8 self_attn layers) - LoRA adapter: trained with Unsloth, r=64, target_modules includes q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj (self_attn), in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z/out_proj (linear_attn), gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj (MLP) - Docker image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0 ### Startup command ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model /model \ --served-model-name Qwen3.5-9B-Base \ --trust-remote-code \ --language-model-only \ --enforce-eager \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 65536 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --enable-lora \ --max-lora-rank 64 \ --max-loras 6 \ --lora-modules 0814=/loras/qwen3.5-9b-nlu-lora-0814 ### Reproduction steps 1. Start vLLM with `--enable-lora` and a Qwen3.5-9B LoRA adapter 2. Send a short prompt ( ~400 tokens) with the LoRA adapter → output is all `!` characters ### Expected behavior LoRA adapter should produce correct output for both short and long sequences, matching: - HuggingFace PEFT `PeftModel.from_pretrained()` inference (works correctly) - Merged model loaded directly in vLLM (works correctly) ### Actual behavior - **Short sequences ( ~400 tokens)**: all output tokens are `!` (token id 0) ❌ - **Base model (no LoRA)**: normal output ✅ - **Merged model in vLLM**: normal output ✅ - **HF PEFT inference**: normal output ✅ The `!` output is caused by NaN in logits: `argmax(NaN) → token 0 → "!"`. ### Root cause analysis This is the same issue described in this CSDN blog post (Chinese): https://blog.csdn.net/qq_26624329/article/details/162686302 ### What I've tried 1. ✅ Changed `torch.empty` → `torch.zeros` in `add_lora_linear` → **still produces `!`** (the bug is deeper than buffer init, likely in `lora_shrink`/`lora_expand` Triton kernels themselves) 2. ✅ `--enforce-eager` → no effect 3. ✅ `--language-model-only` → no effect 4. ✅ Various `--gpu-memory-utilization` values → no effect 5. ✅ Disabled prefix caching / chunked prefill → no effect 6. ✅ Different sampling parameters (temperature, top_p) → no effect 7. ✅ Retrained LoRA with full linear_attn coverage (in_proj_qkv, in_proj_z, out_proj) → no effect ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: MPS: DynamicCache produces NaN logits mid-decode in generate() (transformers >=5.2, regression from 5.0)
items.body: On Apple Silicon (MPS), transformers **>= 5.2.0** produces NaN logits during autoregressive `generate()` with the default cache (DynamicCache), surfacing as: ``` RuntimeError: probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0 File ".../transformers/generation/utils.py", line 2808, in _sample next_tokens = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1).squeeze(1) ``` Setting **`cache_implementation="static"` avoids it entirely**. transformers **5.0.0 is stable** on the identical workload and identical torch; 5.2.0, 5.8.1 and 5.14.1 all reproduce — so the regression entered with the 5.2 cache refactor and is still present. ## Key diagnostic facts Instrumenting `torch.multinomial` in the live failure (rather than a synthetic repro) established: - The failing `generate` is **single-sequence** — `probs.shape == (1, vocab)`, no padding, so this is **not** the fully-masked-row / SDPA-mask issue (pytorch#156707). - The **entire logits row** is NaN (`nan_count == vocab_size`), and it happens **mid-decode** — after ~900 successful sampling steps in the run, not at the first token. - It is **intermittent**: single-shot `generate()` probes (even multi-turn, batched, LoRA, gradient-checkpointed, exact GenerationConfig) never reproduce it; it needs the sustained generation of a real training loop. - **`cache_implementation="static"` completes cleanly** where DynamicCache fails, on the same version/seed/workload — isolating the fault to the dynamic cache path on MPS. ## Environment - Apple M4 Max, macOS (Metal), 48 GB - torch 2.9.1 (constant across all experiments) - transformers 5.2.0 / 5.8.1 / 5.14.1 reproduce; 5.0.0 does not - Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, bfloat16, SDPA, PEFT/LoRA adapter - Workload: TRL 1.8.0 GRPOTrainer tool-calling rollouts (multi-turn generation) ## Reproduction Full repro is a TRL GRPO tool-rollout run (open source: nolabs-ai/hedgehog). A minimal standalone repro has been elusive precisely because the fault needs sustained/pipelined decode pressure — single `generate()` calls always succeed. Happy to run diagnostics on the affected hardware. ## Workaround `cache_implementation="static"` in the generation config. (In isolation this is ~as fast as dynamic; in a loop with varying shapes it recompiles per shape and is ~3x slower without torch.compile — but it is correct.) ## Ask Either the MPS DynamicCache path needs the same numerical guard the static path has, or triage toward the underlying torch MPS behavior if that's where the corruption origin

items.title: [Model] Kimi-K3: all requests degenerate to a repeated token after long-context prefill (NaN logits; packed KDA prefill suspected)
items.body: Serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` at long context reproducibly degenerates: once a large-context request (~240K tokens, well inside the model's 1M-token spec) is processed, the deployment begins returning a **single repeated degenerate token on every step for every subsequent request**, never samples EOS, and every request runs to `max_tokens`. In the observed incident the state persisted ~19 hours and the set of corrupted requests grew over time (2 → 8 concurrent), i.e. the corruption **spreads between requests and is permanent per request** until process restart. items.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 fp8 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): coherent with --enforce-eager, garbage under CUDA graphs — root cause + working fix
items.body: Trying to run MiniMax-M3 with an fp8 KV cache on A100/A800 fails two different ways: 1. `fp8` (e4m3): Triton refuses outright — `type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture`. SM80 can only read `fp8_e5m2` (same conclusion as #3965). 2. `fp8_e5m2`: the server boots, takes a 1M-token window, and generates pure garbage. The garbage is **not** an fp8 precision problem. We measured the e5m2 write/read kernels on SM80 directly: round-trip error 4.5%, full-kernel 12–16% — normal for a 2-mantissa-bit format. The decisive experiment: - `--enforce-eager`: output is perfectly coherent (but 5.2 tok/s — unusable for an 8-TP MoE); - any CUDA-graph mode: garbage. Root cause: the bf16 path writes KV through a fused CUDA op, which is graph-safe. The fp8 path goes through `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` — plain Python that allocates a fresh tensor and does an advanced-index scatter (`idx_cache[slot_mapping] = ...`). Under graph capture that write corrupts the index-K cache, the sparse indexer picks the wrong top-k blocks, and attention reads the wrong KV. This one mechanism explains all three observations (bf16+graph fine, fp8+graph garbage, fp8+eager fine). Fix that works: decorate `_insert_kv` with `@eager_break_during_capture` (the codebase's own idiom for exactly this), route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert), and relax the SM89 guards to SM80. With that, on 8xA800: - full 1,048,576-token window fits (fp8 halves KV; pool ~1.22M tokens); - coherent output; needle retrieval hit at ~100k depth; an 840k-token prompt prefills clean; - ~86 tok/s decode, ≈90% of the bf16 baseline — on SM80 fp8-KV buys memory, not speed; - GPQA Diamond, one harness against both the official API and this build: 93.4% vs 90.9% — quantization costs ≈2.5 pts. Patches, per-kernel probes, and the eval writeup: https://github.com/Hakureirm/minimax-m3-ampere. (#39137's over-broad e5m2 gate is already fixed on main by #45040 — thanks for that.) I am porting the patches onto current main and will open a PR tomorrow. Filing the diagnosis first in case it saves someone the same hunt — and in case a maintainer knows a reason the `eager_break_during_capture` route is wrong here, better before the PR than after. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

DeepGemm E8M0 scale format causes accuracy degradation for this architecture. Falling back to CUTLASS. To disable DeepGemm globally, set VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0. ``` …and then **selects DeepGemm anyway for the MoE layers**: ``` INFO [fp8.py:405] Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['AITER', 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'DEEPGEMM', 'TRITON', 'MARLIN', ...] ``` The auto-disable sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), and `qwen3_5_moe_text` **is** present in `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES` (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) — so the denylist is doing its job. Net effect: the denylist covers dense linear layers only, and the MoE layers — where the accuracy concern for an MoE model actually matters most — still run DeepGemm. So the warning is truthful about dense layers and silently wrong about MoE. ### Why this surfaced now **PR #43477** ("Enable DeepSeek V4 and GLM-5.1 on SM120", shipped v0.24.0) added `is_device_capability_family(120)` to `deep_gemm.py`. items.body: ### Description `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` loads successfully and serves HTTP 200 responses with vLLM 0.26.0, but generated text is semantically corrupted. items.title: [Bug]: Prefill misdispatched into spec-decode FULL cudagraph when prompt length == 1 + num_speculative_tokens → silent GDN state loss, garbage output (hybrid/Qwen3-Next models)
items.body: When speculative decoding is enabled, a **prefill** whose scheduled token count happens to equal `uniform_decode_query_len * num_reqs` is misclassified as a uniform-decode batch and dispatched into the **FULL cudagraph captured for spec-decode**. For hybrid models with GDN/linear-attention layers (e.g. Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-MoE), this silently skips **all recurrent-state writes** for that request: every subsequent decode step then computes from a zero initial state, producing deterministic garbage output and a collapsed draft acceptance rate. The trigger is absurdly easy to hit: with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, **any 3-token prompt** (e.g. the Chinese prompt `中国的首都是` under the Qwen tokenizer) poisons the request from its very first step. I have root-caused this with per-block checksums of the GDN state pools and verified a one-line-of-logic fix. Code on current `main` is identical to what I debugged on 0.27.1. ## Root cause `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) is a **pure shape check**: ```python return ( ((max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len) and (num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs)) if force_uniform_decode is None else force_uniform_decode ) ``` With MTP `k=2`, `uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + 2 = 3`. A virgin single request whose prompt is exactly 3 tokens gives `max_num_scheduled_tokens == 3` and `num_tokens == 3 * 1`, so the **prefill** is classified as uniform decode and `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch(..., uniform_decode=True)` routes it into the FULL graph captured for spec-decode. The failure mechanism for GDN layers: 1. The GDN metadata builder correctly classifies the step as a prefill (`num_prefills=1, num_spec_decodes=0`), **but** the persistent-buffer refresh in `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` only happens in the spec/decode branches (gated on `num_prefills == 0`). A prefill build never touches the persistent buffers. 2. The FULL graph replays with **stale capture-time metadata**: `spec_state_indices_tensor` still holds `0 == NULL_BLOCK_ID` from `build_for_cudagraph_capture`. 3. The FLA kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`) and `causal_conv1d_update` all have null-block guards that **silently skip stores** when the state index is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` — correct padding hygiene, but here it swallows the entire prefill state write. 4. items.body: Hello everyone, I would like to ask my friends a question. After setting up the ` -- bathing-mode dynamic `, I turned on the online inference service. Then two scripts were written, one is the concurrent stress testing script batching_test.py, which is used to send batch requests to the SGLang graph service, simulating multiple people sending requests to the server. Another script, openai_test. py, uses the OpenAi interface to send a single request to the SGLang graph service. However, for the same prompt words, the output images are not the same, and the images generated by batching_test. py for concurrent stress testing scripts have a high probability of distorted lines or missing main characters (which is very common when the prompt words are in Chinese). The image generated by calling the OpenAi interface script openai_test. py will be much better, very fitting the prompt words. I also found that as the number of requests increases, the errors become more severe. I checked the seed and infer_steps, and they are all consistent. To prevent uncertainty, I turned off Cache DiT acceleration. And when I set ` -- batch max size 1 `, the generated image effect will be significantly better, and the result will be the same as the image generated by a single call to the OpenAI interface. items.body: Summary For the kimi_k2 backend in the Streaming Parser Engine, streamed tool-call argument values do not get the schema type coercion ( _fix_arg_types ) that the non-streaming path applies. When the model emits a JSON value whose type differs from the declared tool schema (e.g. "3" for an integer field), non-streaming and streaming clients receive different, differently typed final argument values for the identical model output. Root cause kimi_k2 is the only engine parser with tool_args_json=True and no arg_converter ( vllm/parser/engine/backends/kimi_k2.py:142 ). In vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py : _compute_arg_delta (~line 930-933): when arg_converter is None , returns the raw delta directly and never calls _fix_arg_types . _flush_arg_converter (~line 973-976): same condition, returns None early — no coercion applied on flush either. Non-streaming does coerce: _build_extracted_result calls _fix_arg_types(args_json, name) at ~line 1045. So the arg_converter is None branch (kimi_k2's only branch) skips _fix_arg_types entirely in the streaming path, while the non-streaming path always applies it. items.body: With the default torch.compile/inductor compilation path enabled (`enforce_eager=False`), the CPU MoE kernel path for this architecture produces **NaN logits** for every request, regardless of prompt or endpoint, and **regardless of whether the checkpoint is GPTQ-Int4 quantized or unquantized bf16**. This manifests as: - `/v1/chat/completions` on a simple prompt ("What is 2 + 2? Reply with only the number.") returns a degenerate, repeated `"!"` completion (e.g. `"!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"`) and never reaches EOS — `finish_reason: "length"` even at very low max_tokens. - A raw `/v1/completions` call on `"The capital of France is"` (bypassing the chat template entirely) produces the same degenerate `"!"` output. - Requesting `logprobs=5` on either endpoint surfaces the actual defect: `"Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan"` — the sampled logits are NaN, not merely a bad sample. The model **loads successfully** and passes health/readiness checks (`/health` returns 200) in both cases, which makes this a silent-failure mode worth flagging on its own — a healthy pod/process gives zero signal that generation is broken. **Workaround: `--enforce-eager` completely fixes it, on both checkpoints.** With the identical checkpoint, config, and request, eager mode produces correct, coherent generations with real (non-NaN) logprobs and a proper EOS (`finish_reason: "stop"`). items.title: [Bug]: Streaming vs non-streaming content whitespace mismatch at tool-call boundaries (ParserEngine: qwen3/nemotron_v3/seed_oss/glm47_moe/gemma4)
items.body:
For engine-based parsers, streaming and non-streaming produce **different `content`** for the same model output when plain text sits immediately before, between, or after a tool call. The non-streaming path strips whitespace from tool-associated content (`_strip_content_whitespace` → `content.strip()` in `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`, gated by config flag `strip_content_whitespace_with_tools`, default `True`). The streaming path (`extract_tool_calls_streaming` / `parse_delta` → `_events_to_delta` → `_strip_trailing_reasoning`) has no equivalent step for `delta.content` — `_strip_trailing_reasoning` only trims `delta.reasoning`, and `_events_to_delta`'s own whitespace handling only covers content that is *entirely* whitespace before the first non-whitespace chunk arrives. Boundary whitespace on real (non-whitespace) content adjacent to a tool call is never stripped in streaming. This is not just a synthetic edge case: BPE tokenizers commonly fuse a leading space onto the following word as one token. Verified against the real Qwen3 tokenizer: ```python >>> from transformers import AutoTokenizer >>> tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-8B") >>> tok.encode(" done.") [2814, 13] >>> [tok.decode([i]) for i in tok.encode(" done.")] [' done', '.'] ``` So `" done"` is genuinely emitted as a single token in a real streaming response — this triggers whenever a model emits any prose right before/after a tool call, which is a very common pattern (e.g. "Let me check that for you. ` ...`"). ### Reproduction Environment: offline, no GPU/torch build needed — the parser engine is pure Python. Repro script feeds identical model output through the real streaming path (`extract_tool_calls_streaming`, token-by-token) and the real non-streaming path (`extract_tool_calls`), then diffs `content`. Minimal case (Qwen3, `enable_thinking=False` so pre/post-tool text is `content` not `reasoning`): ```python model_output = ( " 
 
" " Paris 
 
 " " done." ) # fed through streaming as real BPE-like tokens: [..., ' done', '.'] non_streaming_content = "done." streaming_content = " done." # ` opener, a different mechanism. I plan to open a draft PR against this issue with a proposed fix (a streaming post-processor mirroring the existing `_strip_trailing_reasoning` pattern) for early feedback on the approach.

items.title: Mamba2Mixer: use_cache with seq_len > 1 silently produces incorrect results (both CPU and GPU paths)
items.body: Hi, first of all: thank you for your amazing work on incorporating Mamba2 in the `transformers` library. We are researching Mamba for a context in which we have very long sequences, and for computational efficiency we would want to process a sequence in batches (e.g. 10% of the sequence each time). However, we find that this is not supported because `use_cache` (start batch x from the last state of batch x-1) assumes `seq_len=1` (`L=1`), and silently produces incorrect results when `seq_len >1`. # Details: The Mamba2Mixer implementation only implements state carry over when one processes tokens one by one. So it assumes: - `if use_cache` (cached previous state), then it process timesteps one by one - `if not use_cache`, then it uses fast CUDA kernel and process in batch, always starting from initial state. We are missing the option of: - **`use_cache` and process multiple tokens of the sequence at once** In `Mamba2Mixer`: ```python is_decoding = cache_params is not None and cache_params.has_previous_state(self.layer_idx) ``` ### CPU path If `is_decoding=True` it processes only the first input (L=1): `dt = dt[:, 0, :][:, None, ...]` and does a single SSM step instead of a full scan. If we would pass a full sequence into here, it silently only processes the first token, which produces incorrect results. ### GPU path If `is_decoding=True`, it does: ```python _, _, gate, hidden_states_B_C, dt = projected_states.squeeze(1).split( [d_mlp, d_mlp, self.intermediate_size, self.conv_dim, self.num_heads], dim=-1 ) hidden_states_B_C = causal_conv1d_update(hidden_states_B_C, ...) # expects 2D input: (B, conv_dim) ``` The `.squeeze(1)` only removes dim 1 when its size is 1. items.body: ### System Info transformers version: main/latest Platform: all Python version: 3.10+ ### Who can help? @Cyrilvallez ### Information - [ ] The official example scripts - [ ] My own modified scripts ### Tasks - [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...) - [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below) ### Reproduction Steps to Reproduce Run the following code using any model that stores generation cache under a key other than past_key_values : from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf") tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token inputs = tokenizer( "Hello, my dog is cute", return_tensors="pt", ) # Greedy decoding works correctly greedy_out = model.generate( **inputs, num_beams=1, ) print( "Greedy:", tokenizer.decode( greedy_out[0], skip_special_tokens=True, ), ) # Beam search beam_out = model.generate( **inputs, num_beams=3, num_return_sequences=3, ) print( "Beam:", tokenizer.batch_decode( beam_out, skip_special_tokens=True, ), ) Expected Behavior Beam search should produce results that are consistent with the model's cache implementation. During beam reordering, the active cache should be reordered regardless of which cache key name the model uses internally. Actual Behavior Beam search only checks for the presence of: past_key_values before triggering cache reordering. items.title: [Bug] GPTQ gptq_gemm: uninitialized output accumulated into by multi-block atomicAdd (data race, silent wrong results)
items.body: ### GPTQ gptq_gemm: uninitialized output buffer accumulated into by multi-block atomicAdd (data race, silent wrong results) `gptq_gemm` allocates its GEMM output with `torch::empty` (uninitialized) and relies on an in-kernel zero-store that only runs in `blockIdx.z == 0` blocks, guarded by an intra-block `__syncthreads()`. Because the quantized (non-reconstruct) path launches the kernel with `gridDim.z > 1` and every z-block accumulates into the same output element via `atomicAdd` with no cross-block synchronization, this is a data race: blocks with `blockIdx.z > 0` can `atomicAdd` onto uninitialized memory before block `z==0` zeroes it, and the non-atomic zero-store can clobber already-accumulated partial sums (lost updates). Pridyces wrong results (and occasional NaNs) on the small-batch GPTQ decode path. ### Why existing tests don't catch it `sgl-kernel/tests/test_gptq_kernel.py` only runs `use_shuffle=[False]`, and the race is nondeterministic — a fresh `torch::empty` is frequently (but not reliably) zero, so the test passes by luck. ### Failure example Shape `M=8, N=512, K=256, bit=4, use_shuffle=true` → grid `(1, 1, 2)`; both z-blocks write the same `c[m, n]`: 1. Block `z=1` runs first, `atomicAdd`s its `k∈[128,256)` partial onto uninitialized `torch::empty` garbage. 2. Block `z=0` then executes the plain `c = 0` store, **clobbering** z=1's contribution (lost update). 3. Block `z=0` `atomicAdd`s its `k∈[0,128)` partial. Final value omits half the dot product. Separately, a non-atomic 64-bit store racing concurrent `half2` `atomicAdd`s on the same 8-byte region is itself a data race / UB under the CUDA memory model (torn values, possible NaN). ### Reference: vLLM The equivalent vLLM kernel (`csrc/quantization/gptq/q_gemm.cu`) allocates `c` with `torch::zeros` and the in-kernel `// Zero output` is a bare comment (the store loop was removed). vLLM relies entirely on host zero-init. This code was ported from vLLM ("decouple quantization implementation from vLLM dependency") and the `zeros` → `empty` swap is what introduced the bug. ### Severity Silent wrong output (degraded GPTQ accuracy) on the decode path, intermittent and hard to reproduce; occasional NaNs. No crash, so easily missed. ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but

items.body: Qwen-Image-2.1 on the diffusion serving path with `--tp-size 2` produces images corrupted by **dense multicolored (chroma) speckle noise** across smooth regions, while image structure/composition stays correct. The **same prompt/config with `--tp-size 1` is clean**. We also reproduced the identical corruption with vLLM-Omni's independent TP implementation, and verified NCCL numerics across our GPU pair are clean — so this looks like an issue in how this DiT is sharded under TP rather than a hardware/transport problem. ### Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPUs | RTX 5070 Ti (16GB) + RTX 5070 (12GB), both Blackwell `sm_120` | | OS | Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04) | | SGLang | main @ `8ab21c8a9` (2026-09-24), source install with `sglang[diffusion]` | | flash-attn | 2.8.3 self-built for `sm_120` (FA3 wheels ship no sm_120 kernels; pip nvcc + patched CCCL headers) | | Model | Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 (bf16) | ### Reproduce ```bash sglang serve \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-path /root/models/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8094 \ --tp-size 2 --num-gpus 2 \ --performance-mode manual \ --attention-backend fa2 \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload true \ --dit-layerwise-offload true \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 24 \ --vae-cpu-offload true \ --pin-cpu-memory false ``` ```bash curl http://localhost:8094/v1/images/generations -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "prompt": "a ceramic teapot on a wooden table, soft window light, clean background", "size": "1024x1024", "num_inference_steps": 30, "seed": 42, "output_format": "png", "response_format": "b64_json" }' ``` Result: 1024×1024 renders in ~32s but is covered in dense green/purple/orange speckles on smooth surfaces (wall, table, gradients). prs.body: The TRTLLM MHA FP8 KV-cache path was missing part of the scale handoff to FlashInfer. items.body: #47327 (`c4f5cd60d`, "[1/N] Add dense MHA path for sparse MLA short sequences") routes short prefills (`prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`) to a dense-MHA path, so `forward_mqa` now receives only the leading `num_decode_tokens` tokens of the batch instead of all of them. Two parts of the FlashMLA sparse backend were not updated for that new contract: 1. an **out-of-bounds write** in the top-k index conversion whenever the split is active (any kv-cache dtype); 2. the dense-MHA path gathers cached context in a way that does not understand the **`fp8_ds_mla`** cache layout — silently wrong K/V without DCP, hard error with DCP. Both are regressions from #47327: before it, every token went through the MQA path. cc @MatthewBonanni ### Repro ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla ``` **Bug 1 (OOB).** Send concurrent traffic so that a scheduler step holds at least one running decode plus a new short prompt (total seq len ≤ `index_topk` = 2048). The dense-MHA split activates, `forward_mqa` gets only the decode tokens, and the index-conversion kernel writes past the end of its output buffer: non-deterministic corruption of neighbouring GPU allocations, or `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`. Also reproduces with `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (bf16 cache). **Bug 2 (context gather).** Multi-turn chat or any prefix-cache hit, i.e. a prefill that arrives with computed context, total sequence ≤ 2048.
